acceptance_criteria.description: The test creates two distinct authenticated accounts and active leases against one in-process loopback Phase2App, mints two independent one-use realtime tickets, and upgrades two real WebSockets.

After strict initial player-state frames with warp sequences 7 and 41, each client receives PRESENCE_READY before exactly the expected non-self spawn, with distinct nonzero handles and canonical remote identity/state.
A fresh movement state from one client yields an ordered remote update on the peer, and graceful close yields an ordered DISCONNECTED despawn without leaking self events.
All asynchronous operations use deterministic bounded waits and the test tears down its listener and sockets cleanly.
The focused acceptance test, full phase2_http integration target, strict Clippy, formatting, and diff checks pass with the diff confined to the owned test file.

closed_decisions: Use one in-process Phase2App bound to an OS-selected loopback port and seed two one-use invitations through its existing local bootstrap seam; do not weaken the production binary's invitation contract.
Exercise normal register or login, active lease acquisition, ticket minting, one-use ticket upgrade, and strict coop-cloud realtime codecs for both distinct accounts.
Both clients occupy shard 1, channel 1, Hoenn Littleroot but use distinct nonzero warp histories 7 and 41.
Assert PRESENCE_READY precedes remote lifecycle frames, mutual non-self spawn visibility, one ordered update, and DISCONNECTED despawn after a graceful peer close.
Every socket read, write, server-start, and shutdown wait is bounded; tests must not sleep as their primary synchronization oracle.
This unit changes tests only and must not add production bootstrap, transport, credential, or presence behavior.
forbidden_changes: Do not edit production Rust, Cargo files, ROM/Lua/sidecar/launcher code, documentation, generated artifacts, or orchestration state.
Do not bypass authentication or lease fencing, expose tokens in output, hand-roll realtime JSON, loosen frame ordering, use fixed ports, or leave background tasks running after the test.
Do not stage, commit, branch, fetch, pull, push, contact remotes, create or remove worktrees, or revert another worker's edits.
objective: Add a bounded black-box acceptance test proving two separately authenticated accounts exchange Littleroot presence over two real WebSocket connections through one Phase2App server.

return_when: Every acceptance criterion is resolved and all verification outcomes are recorded.
The acceptance test reveals a production defect that cannot be resolved within the owned test file.
A concrete toolchain or isolated-worktree failure prevents progress within the execution budget.
